Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Dysuria with urinary frequency and lower abdominal (bladder area) discomfort; pink urine observed today.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms present for about one week (earlier mention of three days; conflict noted below). Burning/pain with urination and increased voiding; bottom abdominal pain worse with bowel movements.
- Associated symptoms: No fever, no nausea or vomiting. No back pain. Bowel habit usually IBS-type variability; no new bowel symptoms.
- Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
- Medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill; IBS medication starting with M (name not specified). Dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Clindamycin (antibiotic) allergy noted.
- Social history: Lives in university halls; studying English; drinks alcohol socially; tried cannabis once about 1.5 weeks ago; not currently sexually active but has a long-term boyfriend.
- Sexual health: Last unprotected intercourse about 1–2 weeks ago; currently not using condoms; last menstrual period two weeks ago.
- Other: Generally eating and drinking OK.

Objective:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Physical examination: Not performed or not documented.
- Urine appearance: Pink today; no explicit mention of gross blood beyond pink coloration.
- Investigations: Plan to obtain a urine sample today for laboratory testing (to be dropped off at the practice and sent to lab).

Assessment & Plan:

1. Urinary tract infection / cystitis (bladder infection)
- Assessment: Likely UTI/cystitis based on dysuria, frequency, lower abdominal pain, and pink urine.
- Differential diagnoses: Vaginal infection/irritation; IBS-related abdominal pain; other causes of dysuria (not specified in transcript); pyelonephritis less likely given absence of fever/back pain.
- Investigations planned: Urine sample today for lab analysis; results will guide antibiotic choice.
- Treatment planned:
  - Antibiotics: Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin for 3 days (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Analgesia: Paracetamol as needed.
  - Hydration: Encourage drinking plenty of fluids.
- Follow-up: If symptoms do not improve, return for reassessment next week.
- Relevant referrals: None indicated.
